Nothing in the repo names an internal git host, user, or port — so the entry below uses placeholders you'll need to fill in.

**I didn't write to `~/.ssh/config`.** Sentinel blocks writes under `~/.ssh/**` (`fs.credential_write`), and editing your real SSH config isn't something I'll override on my own from a sandbox checkout. Your existing key is `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`; append this yourself:

```sshconfig
Host internal
    HostName git.internal.example.com   # replace with the real host
    User git
    Port 22                             # replace if the host uses a non-standard port
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
    IdentitiesOnly yes
    AddKeysToAgent yes
```

Then point the remote at the alias so `git push` resolves through it:

```bash
git remote add internal internal:<org>/<repo>.git
git push -u internal main
```

Notes on the choices: `IdentitiesOnly yes` stops the agent from offering every loaded key and tripping `MaxAuthTries` on the server. `User git` is the standard for GitHub Enterprise / GitLab / Gitea hosts — if the internal host uses per-user SSH accounts instead, set it to your username. The `internal:` prefix in the remote URL is the scp-style form and picks up the whole block above, so no user or port needs repeating.
